claim: Zebrafish hif-3α gene produces two major transcripts: hif-3α1 (full-length) and hif-3α2 (short variant).
source: RT-PCR analysis of zebrafish embryo RNA detected two major transcripts (Figure 1A). In addition to the previously reported full-length hif-3α transcript (Zhang et al., 2012), there is a short transcript. These transcripts are referred to as hif-3α isoforms 1 and 2, respectively (hif-3α1 and -3α2) hereafter.
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR experimental data shown in Figure 1A and described in the text, and references a prior publication (Zhang et al., 2012).

claim: The hif-3α2 transcript is 893 bp in length and was determined by 5' and 3' RACE with GenBank accession number KR338972.
source: The complete sequence of the hif-3α2 transcript (893 bp) was determined by 5' and 3' RACE (GenBank access number KR338972).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental methodology (RACE) and deposition of sequence data in GenBank.

claim: Hif-3α2 transcript lacks exons 3–10 and a portion of exon 2.
source: It lacks exons 3–10 and a portion of exon 2 (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: The predicted Hif-3α2 open reading frame is 513 bp, encoding a protein of 170 amino acids with a predicted size of 19 kDa.
source: The predicted ORF is 513 bp, encoding a protein of 170 amino acids with a predicted size of 19 kDa.
evidence: The claim is based on computational prediction from the sequence data.

claim: Hif-3α2 protein contains the TAD and LZIP domains but lacks the bHLH, PAS, PAC, and ODD domains.
source: The encoded protein contains the TAD and LZIP domains but lacks the bHLH, PAS, PAC, and ODD domains (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis and domain prediction illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: During early development, hif-3α2 mRNA levels peaked at 9–16 hr post fertilization (hpf), decreased after 20 hpf, and increased again in the larval stage.
source: During early development, hif-3α2 mRNA levels peaked at 9–16 hr post fertilization (hpf), decreased after 20 hpf, and increased again in the larval stage (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: In adult zebrafish, the highest levels of hif-3α2 mRNA were found in the kidney, followed by ovary, spleen, testis, intestine, brain, and heart, with the lowest levels detected in the liver.
source: In the adult stage, the highest levels of hif-3α2 mRNA were found in the kidney, followed by ovary, spleen, testis, intestine, brain, and heart. The lowest levels were detected in the liver (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data from adult tissues shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Hif-3α2 mRNA levels were lower compared with those of hif-3α1 mRNA.
source: Its levels were lower compared with those of hif-3α1 mRNA (Figure 1—figure supplemental 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplemental 1A.

claim: Hif-3α1-GFP was rapidly degraded under normoxia and no GFP signal was observed in embryos injected with Hif-3α1-GFP mRNA.
source: As previously reported, Hif-3α1-GFP was rapidly degraded under normoxia and no GFP signal was observed in this group (Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation and references a prior publication (Zhang et al., 2014).

claim: Strong GFP signal was observed in Hif-3α2-GFP and GFP mRNA injected embryos under normoxia.
source: In contrast, strong signal was observed in Hif-3α2-GFP and GFP mRNA injected embryos (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Hif-3α2-GFP signal was observed in the nucleus, while the GFP protein was present in the cytoplasm and nucleus.
source: The Hif-3α2-GFP signal was observed in the nucleus, while the GFP protein was present in the cytoplasm and nucleus (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data showing subcellular localization in Figure 1E.

claim: Western blotting confirmed that Hif-3α1-GFP was degraded under normoxia while Hif-3α2-GFP was stable.
source: Western blotting confirmed these results (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The Hif-3α antibody detected both Hif-3α1 and Hif-3α2 in HEK293T cells transfected with GFP-tagged constructs.
source: This antibody detected both Hif-3α1 and Hif-3α2 in HEK293T cells transfected with a GFP tagged construct (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting validation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Western blotting results showed comparable levels of Hif-3α2 in zebrafish embryos raised in normoxic and hypoxic water.
source: Western blotting results showed comparable levels of Hif-3α2 in zebrafish embryos raised in normoxic and hypoxic water (Figure 1G), while hypoxia induced a robust increase in Hif-3α1 levels (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data comparing normoxic and hypoxic conditions shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Hypoxia induced a robust increase in Hif-3α1 levels in zebrafish embryos.
source: Western blotting results showed comparable levels of Hif-3α2 in zebrafish embryos raised in normoxic and hypoxic water (Figure 1G), while hypoxia induced a robust increase in Hif-3α1 levels (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data comparing normoxic and hypoxic conditions shown in Figure 1G.

claim: 6 hr, 12 hr, and 24 hr hypoxia treatments did not change Hif-3α2 levels in adult zebrafish.
source: Likewise, 6 hr, 12 hr, and 24 hr hypoxia treatments did not change Hif-3α2 levels in adult zebrafish (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data from adult zebrafish under hypoxia shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Unlike Hif-3α1, Hif-3α2 expression is not regulated by oxygen availability.
source: These results suggest that unlike Hif-3α1, Hif-3α2 expression is not regulated by oxygen availability.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the Western blotting data showing stable Hif-3α2 levels under normoxia and hypoxia.

claim: Co-expression of Hif-3α2 with p2.1 (a HRE reporter construct) resulted in a highly significant, 11.3-fold increase in the reporter activity in HEK293 cells.
source: Co-expression of Hif-3α2 with p2.1, a HRE reporter construct (Semenza et al., 1996), resulted in a highly significant, 11.3-fold increase in the reporter activity in HEK293 cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2A and references a prior publication (Semenza et al., 1996).

claim: The transcriptional activity of Hif-3α2 was abolished when the HRE was mutated (p2.4).
source: This activity was abolished when the HRE was mutated (i.e., p2.4 in Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data comparing wild-type and mutated HRE shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Zebrafish Hif-3α1 caused a 27.4-fold increase in HRE reporter activity in HEK293 cells.
source: In comparison, zebrafish Hif-3α1 and Hif-1α caused a 27.4-fold and 14.5-fold increase, respectively (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Zebrafish Hif-1α caused a 14.5-fold increase in HRE reporter activity in HEK293 cells.
source: In comparison, zebrafish Hif-3α1 and Hif-1α caused a 27.4-fold and 14.5-fold increase, respectively (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Similar HRE-dependent transcriptional activity results were obtained in HeLa cells.
source: Similar results were obtained in HeLa cells (Figure 2—figure supplemental 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data in HeLa cells shown in Figure 2—figure supplemental 1B.

claim: When tagged with GFP and transfected into human cells, Hif-3α2-GFP signal was seen in the nucleus in cultured cells and in zebrafish embryos.
source: When tagged with GFP and transfected into human cells, Hif-3α2-GFP signal was seen in the nucleus in cultured cells and in zebrafish embryos (Figure 2C and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figures 2C and 2E.

claim: Deletion of the TAD abolished the transcriptional activity of Hif-3α2.
source: Deletion of the TAD abolished the transcriptional activity, while it only slightly reduced the nuclear GFP signal intensity (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay and fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: Deletion of the TAD only slightly reduced the nuclear GFP signal intensity of Hif-3α2.
source: Deletion of the TAD abolished the transcriptional activity, while it only slightly reduced the nuclear GFP signal intensity (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: Deletion of the LZIP domain had no effect on the nuclear localization of Hif-3α2 but increased the transcriptional activity.
source: Deletion of the LZIP domain had no effect on the nuclear localization but increased the transcriptional activity (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy and luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figures 2B, 2C, and 2D.

claim: The expression levels of the ΔLZIP mutant were higher than that of Hif-3α and ΔTAD.
source: The expression levels of the ΔLZIP mutant were higher than that of Hif-3α and ΔTAD (Figure 2—figure supplemental 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 2—figure supplemental 1A.

claim: Overexpression of Hif-3α2 in zebrafish embryos resulted in significant increases in the mRNA levels of igfbp-1a, mlp3c, and redd1.
source: Overexpression of Hif-3α2 in zebrafish embryos resulted in significant increases in the mRNA levels of igfbp-1a, mlp3c, and redd1 (Figure 2F–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 2F, 2G, and 2H.

claim: igfbp-1a, mlp3c, and redd1 are known Hif-1α and Hif-3α target genes in zebrafish.
source: These genes are known Hif-1α and Hif-3α target genes in zebrafish (Feng et al., 2012; Kajimura et al., 2006; Kamei et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior publications (Feng et al., 2012; Kajimura et al., 2006; Kamei et al., 2008).

claim: The ΔTAD mutant of Hif-3α2 had no effect on the mRNA levels of igfbp-1a, mlp3c, and redd1.
source: The ΔTAD mutant had no such effect (Figure 2F–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 2F, 2G, and 2H.

claim: The magnitude of induction by Hif-3α2 was much lower compared to that of Hif-3α1 or Hif-1α.
source: The magnitude of induction by Hif-3α2, however, was much lower compared to that of Hif-3α1 or Hif-1α (Figure 2F–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 2F, 2G, and 2H.

claim: Hif-1α increased the expression of its target gene vegfAb, but Hif-3α2 had no such effect.
source: While Hif-1α increased the expression of its target gene vegfAb, Hif-3α2 had no such effect (Figure 2—figure supplemental 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplemental 1C.

claim: Hif-3α1 but not Hif-3α2 increased the mRNA levels of zp3v2 and sqrdl.
source: Likewise, Hif-3α1 but not Hif-3α2 increased the mRNA levels of zp3v2 and sqrdl (Figure 2—figure supplemental 1D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 2—figure supplemental 1D and 1E.

claim: Hif-3α2 is a nuclear protein capable of activating HRE-dependent gene expression in vitro and in vivo.
source: These data suggest that Hif-3α2 is a nuclear protein capable of activating HRE-dependent gene expression in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the combined data on nuclear localization and transcriptional activity.

claim: Hif-3α2 either does not activate the target genes to the same degree or has target genes different from that of full-length Hif-3α1.
source: They also suggest that Hif-3α2 either does not activate the target genes to the same degree or has target genes differ from that of full-length Hif-3α1.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the differential gene expression data.

claim: Overexpression of Hif-3α2 resulted in reduced body growth and developmental timing in zebrafish embryos.
source: Overexpression of Hif-3α2 resulted in reduced body growth and developmental timing in zebrafish embryos (Figure 3—figure supplemental 1A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphometric data shown in Figure 3—figure supplemental 1A–B.

claim: The effect of Hif-3α2 on body growth and developmental timing is similar to what has been reported for the full-length Hif-3α1.
source: This effect is similar to what has been reported for the full-length Hif-3α1 (Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison to a prior publication (Zhang et al., 2014).

claim: The action of Hif-3α2 on body size and somite number appears to require its transcriptional activity.
source: This action of Hif-3α2 appears to require its transcriptional activity because overexpression of the ΔTAD mutant did not change body size or somite number, while the ΔLZIP mutant did (Figure 3—figure supplemental 1A–B).
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the comparison of wild-type and mutant Hif-3α2 effects shown in Figure 3—figure supplemental 1A–B.

claim: Approximately 84% of the Hif-3α2 mRNA-injected embryos had partial or complete loss of myod1-mRNA expressing somites on one or both sides of the body.
source: Approximately 84% of the Hif-3α2 mRNA-injected embryos had partial or complete loss of myod1-mRNA expressing somites on one or both sides of the body (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Similar results to myod1 expression were found with myog mRNA expression in Hif-3α2 overexpressing embryos.
source: Similar results were found with myog mRNA expression (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In ~58% of the Hif-3α2-expressing embryos, spaw expression was detected on the right side, bilaterally, or was completely lost.
source: While the spaw expression was detected on the left side of the body plan in all GFP mRNA-injected embryos, its expression was detected on the right side, bilaterally, or was completely lost in ~58% of the Hif-3α2-expressing embryos (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Similar changes to spaw expression were found with lft2 expression in Hif-3α2 overexpressing embryos.
source: Similar changes were found with lft2 expression (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: During zebrafish development, the shape of the heart changes from a tube-like structure in the middle to a left looped structure.
source: During zebrafish development, the shape of the heart changes from a tube-like structure in the middle to a left looped structure (Stainier, 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to established knowledge (Stainier, 2001).

claim: The cardiac tube remained in the middle or even looped to the right side in half of the Hif-3α2 expressing embryos.
source: The cardiac tube remained in the middle or even looped to the right side in half of the Hif-3α2 expressing embryos (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data showing cardiac tube looping shown in Figure 3E.

claim: No cardiac tube looping phenotype was observed in Hif-3α1 mRNA-injected embryos.
source: No such phenotype was observed in Hif-3α1 mRNA-injected embryos (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: In the control LiPan embryos, the liver was located on the left and pancreas on the right side of the body plan in all embryos.
source: In the control embryos, the liver was located on the left and pancreas on the right side of the body plan in all embryos (Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data in LiPan transgenic embryos shown in Figure 3F.

claim: In the Hif-3α2 group, the liver was found on the right side or in the midline in 28.5% of embryos.
source: In the Hif-3α2 group, the liver was found on the right side or in the midline in many embryos (28.5%) (Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data in LiPan transgenic embryos shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Overexpression of Hif-3α2 but not the full-length Hif-3α1 impairs LR axis development.
source: These data suggest that overexpression of Hif-3α2 but not the full-length Hif-3α1 impairs LR axis development.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the combined data on left-right asymmetry defects.

claim: Kupffer's vesicle (KV) is a transient embryonic organ that plays a key role in establishing the LR asymmetry axis in zebrafish.
source: Kupffer's vesicle (KV), a transient embryonic organ, plays a key role in establishing the LR asymmetry axis in zebrafish (Essner et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to established knowledge (Essner et al., 2005).

claim: The rotating cilia of KV establish a counterclockwise fluid flow and promote intracellular Ca2+ elevation in cells localized on the left side of KV.
source: The rotating cilia of KV establish a counterclockwise fluid flow and promote intracellular Ca2+ elevation in cells localized on the left side of KV, which in turn stimulates the processing and/or secretion of the Nodal-related ligand gene spaw on the left side of KV (Husken and Carl, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to established knowledge (Husken and Carl, 2013).

claim: Hif-3α2 overexpression caused a modest increase in DFC cluster size and total mRNA levels, but these increases were not statistically significant.
source: In situ hybridization and qRT-PCR analyses using the DFC marker gene sox17 indicated that Hif-3α2 overexpression caused a modest increase in DFC cluster size and total mRNA levels, but these increases were not statistically significant (Figure 4A and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 4A and 4C.

claim: There was a slight decrease in the number of migrating DFCs in Hif-3α2 overexpressing embryos.
source: There was a slight decrease in the number of migrating DFCs (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Many Hif-3α2 mRNA-injected embryos had a partially formed KVs (48%) or no KV (20%).
source: While wild-type embryos had normally formed KVs, many Hif-3α2 mRNA-injected embryos had a partially formed KVs (48%) or no KV (20%) (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data using charon marker shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Hif-3α1 overexpression had no effect on KV formation.
source: This action is specific to Hif-3α2 because Hif-3α1 overexpression had no such effect (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Hif-3α2 overexpression causes LR asymmetry defects by impairing KV formation.
source: Taken together, the results suggest that Hif-3α2 overexpression causes LR asymmetry defects by impairing KV formation.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the combined data on KV morphology and LR asymmetry.

claim: Hif-3α2 overexpression resulted in a significant reduction in the mRNA expression of vent and vox.
source: qRT-PCR assays showed that Hif-3α2 overexpression resulted in a significant reduction in the mRNA expression of vent and vox (Figure 4E, F), two genes acting downstream of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway.
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 4E and 4F.

claim: vent and vox are two genes acting downstream of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway.
source: qRT-PCR assays showed that Hif-3α2 overexpression resulted in a significant reduction in the mRNA expression of vent and vox (Figure 4E, F), two genes acting downstream of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the Wnt/β-catenin pathway.

claim: No significant changes were detected in the mRNA expression of the Fgf target gene dusp6, the Hedgehog target gene gli1, or the Notch target gene her4 in Hif-3α2 overexpressing embryos.
source: No significant changes were detected in the mRNA expression of the Fgf target gene dusp6, the Hedgehog target gene gli1, or the Notch target gene her4 (Figure 4—figure supplemental 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplemental 1A–C.

claim: No marked changes were observed in the phospho-Akt and phospho-Erk levels in Hif-3α2 overexpressing embryos.
source: No marked changes were observed in the phospho-Akt and phospho-Erk levels (Figure 4—figure supplemental 1D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 4—figure supplemental 1D–E.

claim: Injection of Wnt3a mRNA into zebrafish embryos resulted in a robust induction in Topflash reporter activity.
source: Injection of Wnt3a mRNA into zebrafish embryos resulted in a robust induction in Topflash reporter activity (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Co-injection of Hif-3α2 abolished the Wnt3a-induced Topflash reporter activity.
source: This induction was abolished by Hif-3α2 co-injection (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Co-injection of Hif-3α2 abolished the induction of Topflash activity by β-cateninΔN.
source: Co-injection of Hif-3α2 also abolished the induction of Topflash activity by β-cateninΔN (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: β-cateninΔN is a constitutively active β-catenin mutant lacking part of the N-terminal sequence.
source: β-cateninΔN is a constitutively active β-catenin mutant lacking part of the N-terminal sequence (Xiong et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a prior publication (Xiong et al., 2006).

claim: The full-length Hif-3α1 did not inhibit Wnt3a- or β-cateninΔN-induced Topflash activity.
source: This action is specific to Hif-3α2 because the full-length Hif-3α1 did not inhibit Wnt3a- or β-cateninΔN-induced Topflash activity (Figure 4—figure supplemental 2A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplemental 2A–B.

claim: Hif-1α had a modest but statistically significant effect on Wnt3a-induced Topflash activity.
source: Hif-1α had a modest but statistically significant effect on Wnt3a-induced Topflash activity (Figure 4—figure supplemental 2A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplemental 2A–B.

claim: Co-injection of Hif-3α2 abolished the Wnt3a- and β-cateninΔN-induced dorsalization phenotype.
source: Co-injection of Hif-3α2 also abolished the Wnt3a- and β-cateninΔN-induced dorsalization phenotype (Figure 4—figure supplemental 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological data shown in Figure 4—figure supplemental 2C.

claim: Wnt/β-catenin signaling regulates KV development and LR asymmetry by stimulating the expression of the ciliogenic transcription factor foxj1a.
source: Wnt/β-catenin signaling has been shown to regulate KV development and LR asymmetry by stimulating the expression of the ciliogenic transcription factor foxj1a (Caron et al., 2012) and the calcium channel cav1.2 (Muntean et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior publications (Caron et al., 2012; Muntean et al., 2014).

claim: Wnt/β-catenin signaling regulates KV development and LR asymmetry by stimulating the expression of the calcium channel cav1.2.
source: Wnt/β-catenin signaling has been shown to regulate KV development and LR asymmetry by stimulating the expression of the ciliogenic transcription factor foxj1a (Caron et al., 2012) and the calcium channel cav1.2 (Muntean et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior publications (Caron et al., 2012; Muntean et al., 2014).

claim: Co-injection of Hif-3α2 mRNA abolished the β-cateninΔN induction of foxj1a and cav1.2 gene expression.
source: Indeed, co-injection of Hif-3α2 mRNA abolished the β-cateninΔN induction of foxj1a and cav1.2 gene expression (Figure 4I–J).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 4I and 4J.

claim: Forced expression of Hif-3α2 but not the full-length Hif-3α1 inhibits Wnt/β-catenin signaling and impairs Kupffer's vesicle development.
source: These results suggest that forced expression of Hif-3α2 but not the full-length Hif-3α1 inhibits Wnt/β-catenin signaling and impairs Kupffer's vesicle development.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the combined data on Wnt signaling and KV development.

claim: The hif-3αΔ42 allele has a 42 bp deletion surrounding the Hif-3α2 ATG site.
source: The hif-3αΔ42 allele has a 42 bp deletion surrounding the Hif-3α2 ATG site (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: The expression of Hif-3α1 mRNA was not affected in the hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos.
source: RT-PCR assays showed that the expression of Hif-3α1 mRNA was not affected in the mutant embryos (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The successful ablation of Hif-3α2 protein was confirmed by Western blotting.
source: The successful ablation of Hif-3α2 protein was confirmed by Western blotting (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The Hif-3α1Δ42 has a 14 aa deletion (residues 456 to 469) located in the N-terminal end of the TAD.
source: The Hif-3α1Δ42 has a 14 aa deletion (residues 456 to 469) located in the N-terminal end of the TAD (Figure 5—figure supplemental 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing and structural analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplemental 1A.

claim: Hif-3α1Δ42 had comparable transcriptional activity to wild type Hif-3α1.
source: When its transcriptional activity was compared with that of the wild type Hif-3α1, Hif-3α1Δ42 had comparable activity (Figure 5—figure supplemental 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplemental 1B.

claim: The expression and functionality of Hif-3α1 protein remain largely unchanged in the hif-3αΔ42 line.
source: These data suggest that the expression and functionality of Hif-3α1 protein remain largely unchanged in the hif-3αΔ42 line.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the RT-PCR and luciferase assay data.

claim: The Topflash reporter activity was significantly elevated in the hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos at 9 hpf compared with the wild-type embryos.
source: Compared with the wild-type embryos, the Topflash reporter activity was significantly elevated in the hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos at 9 hpf (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The mRNA levels of vent and vox were elevated in hif-3αΔ42 embryos at 9 hpf.
source: Likewise, the mRNA levels of vent and vox were elevated in hif-3αΔ42 embryos at 9 hpf (Figure 5F–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 5F and 5G.

claim: A significant increase in Topflash reporter activity was found in the hif-3αΔ20 mutant line compared to wild type embryos.
source: Compared to wild type embryos, a significant increase in Topflash reporter activity was found in the hif-3αΔ20 mutant line (Figure 5—figure supplemental 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplemental 2C.

claim: Endogenous Hif-3α2 negatively regulates the Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
source: These results indicate that endogenous Hif-3α2 negatively regulates the Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the genetic deletion data showing elevated Wnt signaling in mutants.

claim: A most notable phenotype observed in the hif-3αΔ42 mutant line was elevated embryo mortality.
source: A most notable phenotype observed in the hif-3αΔ42 mutant line was elevated embryo mortality (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by mortality data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Many hif-3αΔ42 embryos died before 6–9 hpf.
source: Many hif-3αΔ42 embryos died before 6–9 hpf.
evidence: The claim is supported by mortality data.

claim: The mortality rate in hif-3αΔ42 mutants was significantly higher than that of the wild-type controls.
source: The mortality rate, although varied considerably among different pairs of mutant fish and between different breeding cycles in the same pair (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), was significantly higher than that of the wild-type controls (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by mortality data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The hif-3αΔ20 mutant line also had significantly elevated mortality rate.
source: The hif-3αΔ20 mutant line also had significantly elevated mortality rate (Figure 5—figure supplemental 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by mortality data shown in Figure 5—figure supplemental 2D.

claim: Two out of 105 of the surviving hif-3αΔ42 embryos had reduced forebrain and smaller eyes.
source: Although two out of 105 of the surviving hif-3αΔ42 embryos had reduced forebrain and smaller eyes, most of the surviving hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos looked morphologically normal and continued to develop (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological observation data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Most of the surviving hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos looked morphologically normal and continued to develop.
source: Although two out of 105 of the surviving hif-3αΔ42 embryos had reduced forebrain and smaller eyes, most of the surviving hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos looked morphologically normal and continued to develop (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological observation data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: No difference was detected in the somite development and cardiac looping between the hif-3αΔ42 mutant and wild-type embryos.
source: No difference was detected in the somite development and cardiac looping between the mutant and wild-type embryos (Figure 6C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figures 6C and 6D.

claim: Expression of flh increased at 6 hpf but returned to the control levels at 10 hpf in the hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos.
source: Expression of flh, a mid/caudal diencephalon marker gene, increased at 6 hpf but returned to the control levels at 10 hpf in the hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos (Figure 6E–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figures 6E and 6F.

claim: No difference in pax2a expression was observed between the hif-3αΔ42 mutant and the wild type embryos at 6 and 10 hpf.
source: Meanwhile, no difference in pax2a expression was observed between the mutant and the wild type embryos at 6 and 10 hpf (Figure 6G–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figures 6G and 6H.

claim: Injection of the Hif-3α2 MO but not the control MO reduced the Hif-3α2 protein levels.
source: Injection of the Hif-3α2 MO but not the control MO reduced the Hif-3α2 protein levels (Figure 7A—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Injection of Hif-3α2 MO did not change the levels of Hif-3α1 mRNA.
source: Injection of Hif-3α2 MO did not change the levels of Hif-3α1 mRNA (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Knockdown of Hif-3α2 significantly increased Wnt/β-catenin activity at 9 hpf.
source: Topflash reporter assay and qRT-PCR measurement showed that knockdown of Hif-3α2 significantly increased Wnt/β-catenin activity at 9 hpf (Figure 7B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay and qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 7B, 7C, and 7D.

claim: Many of the Hif-3α2 morphants had phenotypes resembling those of mbl mutant embryos, including the absent or reduced eyes and reduced forebrain.
source: Many of the morphants had phenotypes resembling those of mbl mutant embryos (Heisenberg et al., 2001), including the absent or reduced eyes and reduced forebrain (Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological observation data shown in Figure 7E and comparison to a prior publication (Heisenberg et al., 2001).

claim: The Hif-3α2 targeting MO did not increase embryo mortality at the injected dose (3 ng).
source: These phenotypes were unlikely caused by MO toxicity because the Hif-3α2 targeting MO did not increase embryo mortality nor did it increase p53 mRNA expression at the injected dose (3 ng) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by mortality and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The Hif-3α2 targeting MO did not increase p53 mRNA expression at the injected dose (3 ng).
source: These phenotypes were unlikely caused by MO toxicity because the Hif-3α2 targeting MO did not increase embryo mortality nor did it increase p53 mRNA expression at the injected dose (3 ng) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The hif-3αΔ42 embryos were significantly less sensitive to the Hif-3α2 MO.
source: Furthermore, the hif-3αΔ42 embryos were significantly less sensitive to the Hif-3α2 MO (Figure 7F).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: The expression of boz increased at 6 hpf but returned to the control levels at 9 and 24 hpf in the hif-3αΔ42 mutants.
source: qRT-PCR results showed that the expression of boz, a maternal Wnt signaling target gene (Leung et al., 2003), increased at 6 hpf but returned to the control levels at 9 and 24 hpf in the hif-3αΔ42 mutants (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8A and citation to a prior publication (Leung et al., 2003).

claim: No change was detected in boz expression in the morphants at 6, 9, and 24 hpf.
source: No change was detected in boz expression in the morphants at any of these stages (Figure 8D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: The vent and vox mRNA levels increased significantly at 6 and 9 hpf but these increases disappeared at 24 hpf in the hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos.
source: The vent and vox mRNA levels increased significantly at 6 and 9 hpf but these increases disappeared at 24 hpf in the hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos (Figure 8B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 8B and 8C.

claim: Knockdown of Hif-3α2 resulted in elevated vent and vox mRNA expression at 6, 9, as well as 24 hpf.
source: In contrast, knockdown of Hif-3α2 resulted in elevated vent and vox mRNA expression at 6, 9, as well as 24 hpf (Figure 8E–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 8E and 8F.

claim: A reciprocal decrease in tp63 expression was observed in hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos and morphants.
source: A reciprocal decrease was observed with tp63 expression; tp63 is a direct transcriptional target of Bmp signaling in zebrafish (Bakkers et al., 2002) (Figure 8G–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 8G and 8H and citation to a prior publication (Bakkers et al., 2002).

claim: The hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos have activated certain compensatory mechanisms.
source: These results support the notion that the hif-3αΔ42 mutant embryos have activated certain compensatory mechanisms.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the transient nature of Wnt signaling elevation in mutants versus sustained elevation in morphants.

claim: When treated with Lithium and BIO, a significantly greater portion of the hif-3αΔ42 embryos exhibited the no eye or small eye phenotype compared to the wild type controls.
source: Indeed, when treated with Lithium and BIO, a significantly greater portion of the hif-3αΔ42 embryos exhibited the no eye or small eye phenotype compared to the wild type controls (Figure 8I–J).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological data after chemical treatment shown in Figures 8I and 8J.

claim: Overexpression of Hif-3α2 abolished Wnt3a-induced Topflash reporter activity in HEK293T cells.
source: Overexpression of Hif-3α2 abolished Wnt3a-induced Topflash reporter activity in these human cells (Figure 9—figure supplemental 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data in human cells shown in Figure 9—figure supplemental 1A.

claim: Hif-3α2 had no effect on Wnt5a-induced non-canonical Ap1 reporter activity.
source: In contrast, Hif-3α2 had no effect on Wnt5a-induced non-canonical Ap1 reporter activity (Figure 9—figure supplemental 1B), suggesting that Hif-3α2 only inhibits the canonical Wnt signaling pathway.
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 9—figure supplemental 1B.

claim: Hif-3α2 only inhibits the canonical Wnt signaling pathway.
source: In contrast, Hif-3α2 had no effect on Wnt5a-induced non-canonical Ap1 reporter activity (Figure 9—figure supplemental 1B), suggesting that Hif-3α2 only inhibits the canonical Wnt signaling pathway.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the differential effects on canonical versus non-canonical Wnt reporters.

claim: A truncated human HIF-3α9 (lacking N-terminal 452 residues) had significant HRE-dependent transcriptional activity.
source: We engineered a truncated human HIF-3α9 by deleting its N-terminal 452 residues (Figure 9—figure supplemental 1C). This truncated HIF-3α9, like zebrafish Hif-3α2, had significant HRE-dependent transcriptional activity.
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 9—figure supplemental 1C and 1D.

claim: The truncated human HIF-3α9 (lacking N-terminal 452 residues) inhibited Wnt3a- and β-catenin-induced Topflash activity.
source: It also inhibited Wnt3a- and β-catenin-induced Topflash activity (Figure 9—figure supplemental 1D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 9—figure supplemental 1D–E.

claim: Reciprocal co-IP experiments detected β-catenin and Hif-3α2 in the same complex.
source: Reciprocal co-IP experiments detected β-catenin and Hif-3α2 in the same complex (Figure 9A).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: A direct protein-protein interaction between β-catenin and Hif-3α2 was confirmed by GST pull-down assays.
source: A direct protein-protein interaction between β-catenin and Hif-3α2 was confirmed by GST pull-down assays (Figure 9—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 2A.

claim: No direct interaction was detected between Lef1 and Tcf4 and GST-Hif-3α2.
source: No direct interaction was detected between Lef1 and Tcf4 and GST-Hif-3α2 (Figure 9—figure supplement 2B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 2B–C.

claim: Co-expression of Hif-3α2-GFP decreased the levels of both β-catenin and Lef1 in the immunoprecipitated complex.
source: Co-expression of Hif-3α2-GFP decreased the levels of both β-catenin and Lef1 in the complex (Figure 9B).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Overexpression of Hif-3α2-GFP also reduced the β-catenin and Tcf4 levels in the IP complex.
source: Likewise, overexpression of Hif-3α2-GFP also reduced the β-catenin and Tcf4 levels in the IP complex (Figure 9C).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: The levels of total β-catenin, Lef1, and Tcf4 were all decreased by Hif-3α2 in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Analysis of the Western blotting results of the cell lysates showed that the levels of total β-catenin, Lef1, and Tcf4 were all decreased by Hif-3α2 in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 9B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figures 9B and 9C.

claim: Overexpression of Hif-3α2 had no effect on the levels of Tcf3.
source: Overexpression of Hif-3α2 had no effect on the levels of Tcf3 levels and Hif-3α2-GST failed to pull down Tcf3 (Figure 9—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting and GST pull-down data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 3A–B.

claim: Hif-3α2-GST failed to pull down Tcf3.
source: Overexpression of Hif-3α2 had no effect on the levels of Tcf3 levels and Hif-3α2-GST failed to pull down Tcf3 (Figure 9—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by GST pull-down data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 3A–B.

claim: While Hif-3α2 expression resulted in a marked reduction in β-catenin levels, this reduction was blocked by MG132 treatment.
source: While Hif-3α2 expression resulted in a marked reduction in β-catenin levels, this reduction was blocked by MG132 treatment (Figure 9D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data with proteasome inhibitor treatment shown in Figure 9D.

claim: MG132 treatment also partially inhibited the Hif-3α2-induced reduction in Lef1 levels.
source: Likewise, MG132 treatment also partially inhibited the Hif-3α2-induced reduction in Lef1 levels (Figure 9E).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data with proteasome inhibitor treatment shown in Figure 9E.

claim: MG132 treatment increased Hif-3α2 levels.
source: MG132 treatment increased Hif-3α2 levels (Figure 9D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figures 9D and 9E.

claim: The expression of Hif-3α2 greatly reduced the levels of nuclear β-catenin, while it had a minimal effect on the levels of cytoplasmic β-catenin.
source: The expression of Hif-3α2 greatly reduced the levels of nuclear β-catenin, while it had a minimal effect on the levels of cytoplasmic β-catenin (Figure 9F).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell fractionation and Western blotting data shown in Figure 9F.

claim: Addition of BIO and Lithium, two chemical inhibitors of GSKβ, did not affect the Hif-3α2-induced β-catenin degradation.
source: Addition of BIO and Lithium, two chemical inhibitors of GSKβ, did not affect the Hif-3α2-induced β-catenin degradation (Figure 9G).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data with GSK3β inhibitor treatment shown in Figure 9G.

claim: Hif-3α2 binds to β-catenin and destabilizes the active β-catenin complex through a mechanism that is independent of GSKβ/β-TrCP-mediated degradation.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that Hif-3α2 binds to β-catenin and destabilizes the active β-catenin complex through a mechanism that is independent of GSKβ/β-TrCP-mediated degradation.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the combined biochemical data showing direct binding and GSK3β-independent degradation.

claim: Deletion of the TAD completely abolished HRE-dependent transcriptional activity of Hif-3α2.
source: While deletion of the TAD completely abolished HRE-dependent transcriptional activity (see Figure 2D), it only partially reduced the β-catenin inhibiting activity (Figure 10A).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Deletion of the TAD only partially reduced the β-catenin inhibiting activity of Hif-3α2.
source: While deletion of the TAD completely abolished HRE-dependent transcriptional activity (see Figure 2D), it only partially reduced the β-catenin inhibiting activity (Figure 10A).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 10A.

claim: The ΔLZIP mutant had greater transcriptional activity and full β-catenin inhibitory activity.
source: The ΔLZIP mutant had greater transcriptional activity (see Figure 2D) and full β-catenin inhibitory activity (Figure 10A).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figures 2D and 10A.

claim: Changing L30D31L32 into A (M1 mutant) did not affect the β-catenin inhibitory activity but reduced the HRE-dependent transcriptional activity by half.
source: Changing L30D31L32 into A (i.e., M1 mutant) did not affect the β-catenin inhibitory activity but reduced the HRE-dependent transcriptional activity by half (Figure 10A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figures 10A and 10B.

claim: Mutant M2 (changing D44F45Q46 into A) had partial β-catenin inhibitory activity and retained half of its HRE-dependent transcriptional activity.
source: Mutant M2 (changing D44F45Q46 into A) had partial β-catenin inhibitory activity (Figure 10A), while it retained half of its HRE-dependent transcriptional activity (Figure 10B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figures 10A and 10B.

claim: The A36G mutant had full β-catenin inhibitory activity but completely lost its transcriptional activity.
source: The A36G mutant had full β-catenin inhibitory activity (Figure 10A), but completely lost its transcriptional activity (Figure 10B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figures 10A and 10B.

claim: Changing P37 to A eliminated both β-catenin inhibitory activity and HRE-dependent transcriptional activity.
source: Changing P37 to A, however, eliminated both activities (Figure 10A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figures 10A and 10B.

claim: All three mutants possessing full β-catenin inhibitory activity (ΔLZIP, M1, and A36G) strongly induced β-catenin degradation.
source: All three mutants possessing full β-catenin inhibitory activity, i.e., ΔLZIP, M1, and A36G, strongly induced β-catenin degradation (Figure 10C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: P37A, which had no β-catenin inhibitory activity, had no impact on β-catenin stability.
source: P37A, which had no Figure 10C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: M2 and ΔTAD, which had partial β-catenin inhibitory activity, had a modest impact on β-catenin stability.
source: M2 and ΔTAD, which had partial β-catenin inhibitory activity, had a modest impact on β-catenin stability (Figure 10C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: Human HIF-3α9Δ1–452 had similar activity in destabilizing β-catenin.
source: Human HIF-3α9Δ 1–452 had similar activity in destabilizing β-catenin (Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 2.

claim: Overexpression of A36G and Hif-3α2 resulted in heart randomization and abnormal somite development.
source: Overexpression of A36G and Hif-3α2 resulted in heart randomization and abnormal somite development (Figure 10D, E).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figures 10D and 10E.

claim: Overexpression of P37A, which lacks the ability to induce β-catenin degradation, had little effect on heart randomization and somite development.
source: In contrast, overexpression of P37A, which lacks the ability to induce β-catenin degradation, had little effect (Figure 10D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figures 10D and 10E.

claim: Hif-3α2 alters LR asymmetry by destabilizing β-catenin and this action is independent of its HRE-dependent transcriptional activity.
source: These findings suggest that Hif-3α2 alters LR asymmetryby destabilizing β-catenin and this action is independent of its HRE-dependent transcriptional activity (Figure 10F).
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the mutant analysis data showing separation of transcriptional and β-catenin degradation activities.
